req.title: Create task
req.statement: The system shall create a new task and respond with HTTP 201 and the created task body when POST /tasks/ receives a valid TaskCreate payload.
expected_outcomes: response body includes id, title, completed=false

doc.reasoning: The requirement mandates that POST /tasks/ with a valid TaskCreate payload returns HTTP 201 and a body containing id, title, and completed=false. I designed: (1) a positive EP test with a fully valid payload asserting exact status code 201 and all response fields; (2) a negative NEG test with a missing required 'title' field asserting HTTP 422 (FastAPI validation error, not 201); (3) a BVA boundary test with a title of exactly 1 character (minimum allowed by min_length=1) asserting 201 and correct echo; (4) a BVA boundary test with a title of exactly 100 characters (maximum allowed by max_length=100) asserting 201; (5) a BVA boundary test with a title of 101 characters asserting 422 (over the max); (6) a DT test with completed=true explicitly set, asserting the response reflects the provided value; (7) a NEG test with an empty string title asserting 422. These collectively kill mutations on status code constants, field presence checks, boolean defaults, and string length boundary comparisons.

tests.name: test_create_task_valid_payload_returns_201_with_body
actions: POST /tasks/ with valid JSON body {title: 'Buy groceries', description: 'Milk and eggs', completed: false}
trace: R-TASK-001: valid payload -> HTTP 201 + task body
tests.executable:
import os, sys
os.environ.setdefault('DATABASE_URL', 'sqlite:///./test_r_task_001_ep.db')
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker
from app.database import Base
from app.main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

test_db_path = './test_r_task_001_ep.db'
if os.path.exists(test_db_path):
    os.remove(test_db_path)
engine = create_engine('sqlite:///' + test_db_path, connect_args={'check_same_thread': False})
Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)

client = TestClient(app)

def test_create_task_valid_payload_returns_201_with_body():
    payload = {'title': 'Buy groceries', 'description': 'Milk and eggs', 'completed': False}
    r = client.post('/tasks/', json=payload)
    assert r.status_code == 201
    body = r.json()
    assert isinstance(body['id'], int)
    assert body['id'] > 0
    assert body['title'] == 'Buy groceries'
    assert body['description'] == 'Milk and eggs'
    assert body['completed'] == False
    assert 'created_at' in body

tests.executable:
import os
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from app.database import Base
from app.main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

test_db_path = './test_r_task_001_ep_id.db'
if os.path.exists(test_db_path):
    os.remove(test_db_path)
engine = create_engine('sqlite:///' + test_db_path, connect_args={'check_same_thread': False})
Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)

client = TestClient(app)

def test_create_task_response_id_is_positive_integer():
    r1 = client.post('/tasks/', json={'title': 'Task One'})
    assert r1.status_code == 201
    body1 = r1.json()
    assert isinstance(body1['id'], int)
    assert body1['id'] >= 1
    r2 = client.post('/tasks/', json={'title': 'Task Two'})
    assert r2.status_code == 201
    body2 = r2.json()
    assert isinstance(body2['id'], int)
    assert body2['id'] >= 1
    assert body2['id'] != body1['id']
